title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a short transitional page. It finishes Remark 3 from the previous page, then opens a new section 9.

End of Remark 3. The previous page set up a datum (X, (X_i)_{i in I}, (B_alpha, E_alpha)_{alpha in Lambda}): a space with a closed stratification indexed by a finite poset I, plus a family of 'cylinder' data (bases B_alpha with fibrations or tubes E_alpha). Remark 3 says one could instead give a cylindrical stratification of a given type on X. This page adds three things:
- That variant 'makes no essential difference to the treatment given here.'
- Later the notion of (global) cylindrical stratification will be generalised to a local one.
- The same work will then be seen to apply.

The global version means one tubular or cylindrical structure along each closed stratum union. The local version means such structures exist only locally over the strata, in the spirit of local triviality.

Section 9 heading: 'Description of a conic stratification of type I (I a finite ordered set).' The word 'structure' is crossed out and replaced by 'stratification'. Grothendieck then simplifies: he first treats the case where the data are given by cylindrical stratifications on X itself, apparently without passing through models (reading uncertain). The page ends with a struck-out 'Soit'.

The next page carries out the programme. It gives a 'standard presentation' of an equisingular stratification of type I as a functor Sigma : Drap(I) -> M, where Drap(I) is the category of flags (chains) of I and M is a 'model' topological category. The conditions are:
- restriction to an initial segment of a flag is a fibration;
- deleting a non-final index is a boundary (cylindrical) embedding.

In modern terms, the problem served is to build the 'unfolding' (déploiement) of a stratified space. Each chain i_0 < ... < i_n gets a manifold-with-corners-like piece, namely the iterated link bundle. These pieces are glued along fibrations and boundary embeddings, in the manner of Thom–Mather control data and Mather's abstract stratified sets. Today the closest analogues are the resolution or unzipping of conically smooth stratified spaces (Ayala–Francis–Tanaka) and the diagrammatic description of stratified spaces over the poset of flags.

This page itself contains only announcements and a section title, with no mathematical content to check beyond that.

ideas.what: Passage from global cylindrical stratifications (a global tube/cylinder structure along strata) to local cylindrical stratifications
ideas.modern_name: Locally given control data / local conic structure (Thom–Mather control data, Siebenmann locally cone-like stratified spaces)
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme (dévissage of stratified structures, tame topology) is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6

ideas.what: Conic stratification of type I for a finite poset I, to be described via cylindrical stratification data (leading on the next page to a functor on the flag category Drap(I))
ideas.modern_name: Conically stratified spaces over a poset; unzipping / link-bundle description indexed by chains of the poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mather (abstract stratified sets), Lurie (Higher Algebra Appendix A, conically stratified spaces), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (conically smooth, unzip)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions 'dévissage' of stratified structures in tame topology, but not this formalism in detail

deep.surprise_reason: Transitional page: a programmatic remark (global to local cylindrical stratifications) and a section heading. The substantive flag-category presentation is on the next page; nothing here goes beyond known stratification theory.
transcription_corrections: Line 'on prend [?] le cas' likely reads 'on prend d'abord le cas': the inserted word 'd'abord' is written below the line with a caret, rather than 'ordonné' being inserted in the parenthesis '(I un ensemble fini)'.

Final line 'driques sur X par ensembles ordonnés [?]' seems instead to read roughly 'driques sur X pas besoin des modèles' (or similar). This suggests the simplified case avoids the model category introduced on the next page; reading uncertain.
End of first paragraph 'et on verra le même [?] travail [?]' is uncertain; possibly 'et on verra la même chose'.
Section title: 'structure' is crossed out and 'stratification' written above, so the title reads 'Description d'une stratification cônique de type I'.
